DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City vavw_dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 126 s. 2022 October 10, 2022 HON. ARMI DELA CRUZ CARRION Mayor Boac, Marinduque Dear Mayor Carrion: This has reference to your letter dated July I, 2022 regarding the propriety of hiring within the one-year prohibition of losing candidates on the job order or contract of service basis. Based on your letter, it appears that you have already came across the following: 1) CSC Resolution No. 02-0012 relative to said Commission's response to then Batanes Governor Vicente S. Gato; and 2) DILG Region XIII Legal Opinion No. 2016-032. In both instances, the CSC and DILG Region XIII stated that the hiring of losing candidates on job order or contract of service status may be allowed within the one- year prohibition given that contract of services and job orders are not considered government serv'ice nor is there an employee-employer relationship between the hired person and the institution. Hence, your query. Per verification, pertinent portion of the aforesaid DILG 13 Legal Opinion No. 2016- 032 reads: "Under CSC Memorandum Circular No. 38, s. 1993 (now reproduced under Rule XI, Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Actions/CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998), services rendered under contracts Of services and iob orders are not considered qovernment services; and contracts do not have to be submitted to the CSC for approval; the employees involved in the contract or iob orders do not enjoy the benefits enioyed by government employees such as PERA, COLA and RATA; no employer-employee relationship exists; and they are not covered bv civil service law. Based on the foregoing, we can logically infer that those employed on job order basis do not hold a public appointive office within the contemplation of Civil Service law and rules. Thus, hiring on iob order basis of non-winninq candidates in an election may bc allowed. This has also been pronounced in CSC RESOLUTION NO. 02-0012 dated January 3, 2002." "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

could be gleaned from the foregoing, our DILG-Region XIII based its stand on Memorandum Circular No. 38, s. 1993 and Resolution No. 02-0012 dated January 3, 2002, both issued by the Civil Service Commission (CSCI. It bears pointing out, however, that on February 15, 2011, the CSC, in Resolution No. 1100267 in the case of Mr. Aurelio Salunat, already deviated from their ruling. In this CSC Resolution No. 1100267, said Commission admitted that in the earlier case of Gato, Vicente S. Re: Query: Hiring of Non-winning Election Candidates on Job Order Basis (CSC Resolution No. 02-0012 dated January 3, 2002) and the case of Melendez, Amador O. (CSC Resolution No. 01-1606 dated October 4, 2001), the Commission still ruled that the hiring on job order basis of non-winning candidates in an election may be allowed, considering that job order contract is not an appointment within the contemplation of Civil Service Law and rules. The CSC's rationale at that time was that the prohibition is not defeated considering that the services of a consultant are not directly delivered to the people who rejected him/her but more to the person who hires him/her. In fact, the CSC declared that its earlier ruling in Gato and Melendez cases may still be applied in the Salunat case [subject of CSC Resolution No. 11002671 since the Commission has not yet changed its position on the matter. However, the CSC's deviation in Resolution No. 1100267 from its earlier ruling in Gato and Melendez cases came into place with the Commission's realization that the salaries of those hired under contract of service and job order basis are drawn from public funds so that there is an issue of the propriety of paying for the services of a losing candidate out of public fund. Let it be noted that the non-winning election candidate subject of CSC Resolution No. 1100267 was engaged as a consultant on legislation in the Municipality of Quezon. Although it was not clearly stated in the CSC Resolution that the consultant's remuneration shall be taken from public funds, this can be deduced from the nature of his engagement, that is, in the "legislation in the Municipality of Quezon" which obviously, shall inure to public welfare. Quoting the Commission in its CSC Resolution No. 1100267, viz: "xxx salaries of those hired under contract of service and job order basis are drawn from public fund. Thus, there is an issue of the propriety Of paying for the services of a losing candidate out of In the CSC ruling, it was stressed that the service of a non-winning candidate as a consultant is not directly delivered to the people who rejected him/her in an election but more to the person who hires him/her. Thus, it should be the responsibility of the person who hires a non-winning candidate as consultant to pay for his/her salary and should not be taken from the public fund. Moreover, if such action continues to be allowed, it may create a scenario wherein an unwanted or indirect discharge of duties would exist. This would in effect result to an indirect or strategic way of putting back into office a non-winning candidate and making him/her discharge functions without the mandate of the electorate. xxx Page 2 of 3

From all of the foregoing, it follows that employing non-winning candidates through contract of service or job order may be considered as a means of circumventing Civil Service Law and rules on appointment, particularly the rule prohibiting the appointment of a person who lost in an election within one year following such election. WHEREFORE, the Commission hereby rules that the hiring on job order basis of non-winning candidates in an election is tantamount to circumvention of Civil Service Law and rules, particularly the rule prohibiting the appointment of a person who lost in an election within one year following such election." (Emphasis Supplied) Since the CSC already deviated from its ruling, so must the DILG, which only relied in the former. In this regard, DILG 13 Legal Opinion No. 2016-032 is hereby revoked. It is hereby opined, based on CSC Resolution No. 1100267, that the hiring on job order basis of non-winning candidates in an election where their salaries are drawn regardless of fund source is tantamount to circumvention of Civil Service Law and rules, particularly the rule prohibiting the appointment of a person who lost in an election within one year following such election. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you.
